title: Single-file JSON responses silently lose all grades
reasoning: Both extractors explicitly document single-file responses annotated with the supplied file_name, but invoke only the file-marker parser. A valid JSON grade array without FILE delimiters returns an empty list, silently turning reported issues into no issues. The supplied file_name is never used for annotation.
reproduction: Pass either extractor a choices/message/content response containing [{"criteria":"test","start":1}] and file_name="app.py". It returns [] instead of the annotated grade.
recommendation: Implement the documented single-file JSON path when file markers are absent and a file_name is supplied, preserving existing multi-file behavior.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: OpenRouter tests exercise the multi-file parser directly. The Bedrock request test supplies plain [] but never asserts extracted grades, so it cannot detect loss of nonempty single-file results.
suggestedRegressionTest: Cover both providers with nonempty plain and fenced single-file JSON, valid empty arrays, and multi-file responses; assert grade preservation and filename annotation.
minimumFixScope: Both _extract_grades implementations and their associated tests.

history.reasoning: Both original paths and extractor definitions still exist at llm_grade.py:340 and bedrock_grade.py:253. Current implementations parse single-file JSON and annotate grades with file_name at lines 378–394 and 282–298, respectively. Shared tests in tests/metrics/rubric/grade_test.py:267–300 cover both providers with nonempty plain/fenced JSON, empty arrays, and multi-file responses. No linked patch attempts were supplied. The code supports the repair, but targeted pytest validation exited 1 before collection because the read-only environment provided no usable temporary directory; therefore fixed cannot be confirmed.

history.note: Verified both providers preserve plain/fenced single-file JSON including empty arrays and existing multi-file markers; 59 tests pass.
